description: SpaceMiT K3: 16 riscv64 harts on shared memory. X100 = harts 0-7 (VLEN=256), A100 = harts 8-15 (VLEN=1024). Facts below were measured on the board.

notes.clusters: X100 = CPUs 0-7, A100 = CPUs 8-15. L2 is shared per group of 4 cores (0-3 and 8-11 confirmed by measurement). /proc/cpuinfo reports the same ISA string on all 16 harts, so the core type is not discoverable from it.
notes.vlen: X100 vlenb=32 (VLEN 256); A100 vlenb=128 (VLEN 1024). Both are legal for zvl256b, which is only a lower bound.
notes.a100_isa: The A100 runs backend ime_k3_a100 (-march=rv64gcv_zvl1024b_zfh_zvfh; lineage ime_k3_a100 -> rvv_k3_a100 -> rvv). Hand-written IME (smt.vmadot 8x16x8) kernels live in kernels/ime_k3_a100/; every op without one falls through to the tuned kernels in kernels/rvv_k3_a100/ and then the shared rvv set, all compiled at zvl1024b. zvl1024b (not zvl256b) because GCC at zvl256b can emit whole-register spills with VLEN-256-sized stack slots that overrun on VLEN=1024. zvl1024b code is ILLEGAL on the X100. Each core's `backend` field names the backend its kind runs.
notes.ai_thread_cpus: Threads that run on the A100 must write their TID to /proc/set_ai_thread (done by the runtime, never from a shell). Registration is ONE-WAY: there is no unregister, so a thread that has joined the A100 pool stays there. The process itself starts on the X100 (taskset -c 0-7) and A100 worker threads self-register. `ai_thread_cpus` lists the harts that need this; build scripts pass it as AI_CPUS= / -DMODELBLASTER_AI_CPUS= in compact form (e.g. 8-15).
notes.clock: rdtime is unprivileged and runs at 24 MHz, same as the K1. Timing must convert with 24 MHz, never the core clock.
notes.core_kind: X100 and A100 are DISTINCT kinds (x100 / a100) even though they share one capability list (their backends differ: x100 -> rvv_k3, a100 -> ime_k3_a100). `kind` is what _resolve_target uses to pick a hart -- the n-th core OF THAT KIND -- so one shared kind would make CPU_E#n alias CPU_P#n and double-book harts 0-7 (see the K1 notes). Here CPU_P = x100, CPU_E = a100.
notes.ime: No ime_* capability is declared: the K3 IME has not been characterised, and the K1 smt.vmadot facts do not transfer.
notes.ime_presence: Measured 2026-11 (scripts/k3_ime_presence_probe.c, artifacts/k3_probes/ime/): vmadot (.insn r 0x2b,f3,0x71) EXECUTES on ALL 16 CPUs (X100 0-7 and A100 8-15): signed/unsigned/us/su all execute. int4 (funct7 0x61) executes on A100 only (SIGILL on X100). LMUL=2 and odd vd trap (SIGILL) everywhere. vl is ignored (any vl 1..VLMAX gives the full-tile result), unlike K1 which needed vl=32.
notes.ime_tile_a100: A100 (vlenb 128) int8 tile M=8,K=16,N=8; X100 (vlenb 32) tile M=4,K=8,N=4. Layout verified bit-exact (20000 random trials x 4 sign variants, accumulate onto nonzero C): A[i*K+k] (vs1, v-reg bytes row-major MxK), B[j*K+k] (vs2, N x K i.e. B transposed), C[i*N+j] int32 row-major across concatenated (vd | vd+1), vd even, C += A.B^T. funct3 3=s*s, 0=u*u, 1=A unsigned*B signed, 2=A signed*B unsigned. int4 (A100 f7=0x61): 8x32x8, signed nibbles, low nibble = lower k. See artifacts/k3_probes/ime/summary.md.
notes.ime_throughput: vmadot int8 peak (8 independent accumulator pairs, regs preloaded): A100 0.69 ns/instr = 1480 MAC/ns (int4 ~3000), latency 4.5 ns (chain); X100 0.49 ns = 262 MAC/ns, latency 2.3 ns. vs vwmacc i8->i16 57 (A100) / 34 (X100) MAC/ns: 26x / 7.7x at peak. With L1 operand loads in the loop A100 is load-bound (vle8 128B ~5.3 ns, ~25 B/ns): 2x4 tile blocking gives ~213-265 MAC/ns (A100), ~150 (X100). Need >=4 independent accumulators.

cores.name: x100_core0
cores.description: X100, VLEN=256 (vlenb=32). L2 domain shared with harts 0-3. RVV only; no IME capability.

cores.name: a100_core8
cores.description: A100, VLEN=1024 (vlenb=128). L2 domain shared with harts 8-11. Treated as X100-ISA-only (zvl256b) for now; kernels must be VL-agnostic.
